data.turoyo: Annaqqa bad dukkane, azzən u Ḥannayḏan w 3-4 man naʕime, u Ḥannayḏan u muxtar, u Ḥanna u barḥəmayḏi. 3-4 man naʕimayḏan mḥaǧaǧǧe aʕlayye.
data.translation: Then at the shops our Hanne and three or four young men went, our Hanne the mukhtar, and Hanne my brother-in-law. Three or four of our young men had argued with them.

rationale: Thin II.1 Preterit cell and unusual plural mḥaǧaǧǧe with ʕal-target; preserves the pharyngeal consonant and final cluster. English is the supplied project machine translation.

summary: No accepted change to the numbered sense or form inventory. Existing41/14 securely illustrates II dispute/find a pretext with ʕal target.

Allowed lookup hyǧ has hayəǧ/hoyəǧ excited; no hǧǧ entry. Form lookup gives exact mḥaǧəǧ underḥǧǧ, while the non-pharyngeal expanded mhaǧǧiǧinale has no exact attestation and surfaces only as a loose match. This does not decide the derivative or its root.
The attack clause in JTM5.2/49 supports contextual provoking, but ḥǧǧ versus a possible hyǧ derivative remains unresolved. Do not silently normalise h toḥ or simplify consonant length.
mḥaǧaǧǧe is provisionally II Preterit with plural-agent assimilation. The English had argued does not establish a participle or a Preterit-wa.
No new provoking/causing-anger sense is inferred. Jan's disputing frame fits the existing sense and does not overturn the unresolved round-1 root identification.
Verify the recording/edition's mhaǧǧiǧinale in JTM5.2/49: root, h/ḥ, repeated ǧ, vowels and stem.
If the form belongs toḥǧǧ, does it mean disputing/taunting with attack inferred, or a distinct causative provoking sense? No new form is proposed before that check.
Confirm mḥaǧaǧǧe as an agent-suffixed II Preterit, rather than a participial predicate; verify the printed final ǧǧe cluster without normalizing it.
A plural human subject disputes with an aʕlayye target, directly confirming the inherited ʕal government. This securely spelled mḥ- token does not resolve round 1's non-pharyngeal mhaǧǧiǧinale.
